inline_text:
Follow-up to a read of the repo's `gws` wrappers, then a six-agent self-review of that follow-up. Everything was green before either pass: 486 lib tests, every skill test, all nine repo guards. None of them could see any of this.

## The one that can corrupt the estate

Six call sites sent `drive.files.create`, `drive.files.copy`, `appendDimension`, `insertDimension` or `addSheet` at the default five attempts. A request that succeeded server-side but answered like a timeout is indistinguishable, from here, from one that never landed — so the retry makes a **second folder, file, column or tab**. Nothing downstream detects it: the next `list_children` reports a subtree holding everything twice and the rebrand walks both; a verify that reads by header name finds the names it asked for; Sheets does not refuse a duplicate tab title, it renames the second one so the exists-check never matches again.

`sync_badges.py` had already learned this at its two write sites. The rule has one definition now — `aaif_events.gws.NO_RETRY` — and, because a keyword at a call site is opt-in and opt-in shipped with four counterexamples already in the tree, **`scripts/check_non_idempotent_retries.py`** is the counterexample detector. Exact for Drive (both the positional and the argv-list shape; missing the second would have left `sync_badges.upload_new` unguarded), module-level for Sheets, where the request key is built in a different function from the call that sends it.

## Why the private wrappers were there, and why that stopped being true

Each local copy sat behind a *"Local so this script stays standalone"* comment. But `aaif-create-chapter`, `aaif-sync-badges` and `aaif-sync` were all already on the README's not-zippable list, because a **sibling** script in the same folder imports `lib`. The zip was already broken. What was left was drift:

| | retry table | scrubs output | non-idempotent writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aaif_events.gws` | 11 substrings + boundary-matched statuses | yes | caller's call |
| `sync_badges.py` | **5** substrings | no | guarded |
| `create_chapter.py` | 9 + bare `"500"` substring | no | **unguarded** |
| `create_series.py` | 9 + bare `"500"` substring | **no** | **unguarded** |
| `slides_export.py` (inside `lib`) | 9 + bare `"500"` substring | partly | **unguarded** |
| `install_ops_notes.py` | **none — bare `subprocess.run`** | no | **unguarded** |

All five copies are gone. `create_series.py` is the interesting one: it kept its copy *specifically* to stay zippable for claude.ai, and that copy had fallen two fixes behind — including that it interpolated the child's raw stdout+stderr into its exceptions. `gws` dumps its environment on some failures and the scrub deliberately keeps `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLI_*` because `gws` needs it, so an OAuth client secret and refresh token are exactly what such a dump holds, out of the skill most likely to be run by someone who pastes the traceback into a public issue. A copy nobody can keep in step is worse than the coupling it avoids, so the skill takes the coupling.

## Also fixed

- **The env scrub had narrowed.** `AAIF_SLACK_\w*_TOKEN` requires a middle segment, so a bare `AAIF_SLACK_TOKEN` — which the `startswith`/`endswith` copies matched — survived into every `gws` child. Nothing sets that spelling today.
- **A failure names the verb and never the payload.** It was `gws failed (1): …` out of scripts issuing a dozen calls across two spreadsheets, and it folded in the child's stdout, where a `values.get` that streams half its rows and then exits nonzero puts those rows. Now `gws sheets spreadsheets batchUpdate failed (1): …`, from stderr only.
- **`install_ops_notes.py` read "no JSON" as "empty sheet".** That surfaced as "no tab titled X — a rename, not an empty sheet" (ruling out what happened), "X has no header row" (of a tab that has one), or "wrote Ops Notes but a fresh read does not show it" after a write that landed — and re-running on that last one issues a second `appendDimension`, reaching the duplicate column the guard prevents by the long way round. Only the two writes tolerate silence now.
- **Both cloners abort with a sentence, not a traceback.** The estate was already recoverable (temp dir cleaned, "Done" never printed, `--resume` adopts an orphan by name); nothing told the operator so.
- **`check_portable_skills.py` reads imports, not substrings**, as its own docstring said to do the first time a file merely *mentioned* `aaif_events`. A dynamic import aborts rather than reading as portable.

## Checks

- 493 lib tests (+8), every skill test, `pre-commit run --all-files`, `claude plugin validate .` — all pass. No live run; everything is exercised against mocked subprocesses.
- **Mutation-tested, because the first version of these tests was not a test.** Asserting `retries=NO_RETRY` in `call_args.kwargs` passes even when the argument is discarded a layer below: dropping the pass-through in `gws.json_out` left the guard inert with all 486 tests green. Every guarded site now drives a counted subprocess, and ten mutations — dropping the budget at each layer, changing `NO_RETRY`, breaking `max(1, retries)`, un-guarding each call site, re-narrowing the env scrub — are each caught. The new check was mutation-tested the same way against all seven files.
